items.title: Eblen Rau Interview, 1974-05-27
items.q: He lived right around the corner from where I was living at that time... That was Fritz, or Fred as we called him.

ctx.x: You may be talking about somebody else. This is at the Miramar, I think. I think Benji White told me about him. Well? Fred Ogden? Fred Ogden.

It was Fred Ogden, Benji White, Monk Smith. Oh, not Dybal, I know who you're talking about. Debal. Debal. Debal. He was the architect. He was the architect. He was the worst musician we had. He didn't claim to be much of a musician, but Fritz Ogden used to tell him, remember, six, five, three, and he would change his chord when he was playing on the thing. That's the only reason he knew how to change it. They had him fixed up that way. But he got along all right. But that was Jinx.

items.title: Eblen Rau Interview, 1974-05-27
items.q: He could tell these funny stories that went along with our type of entertainment there... That was the little Frenchman played the banjo.

ctx.x: And he had a good ear for changes? Yeah, he had a good ear.

But he also had a nice sense of humor. He could tell these funny stories that went along with our type of entertainment there. But if I'm not mistaken, Fritz at that time was playing the banjo or some kind of makeshift banjo, banjo mandolin or something, I don't know what the hell they called it. I don't think it was a straight banjo. That was the little Frenchman played the banjo. Oh, I know who you're talking about. Five string, a four string, a six string? I think he had a six string. He could play a damn…
Was this before Rene Jelpie or after him?
